one_liner: Single-header C++11 ziggurat sampler meant to replace std::normal_distribution; the repo publishes no speed numbers.
what_it_does: Provides cxx::ziggurat_normal_distribution<T>, a class template with the RandomNumberDistribution interface (param_type, mean/stddev, operator() with or without params, stream operators). Code written for std::normal_distribution<T> can switch to it, and it works with any standard URNG such as std::mt19937_64. It handles the normal distribution only.
how_it_is_fast: Marsaglia-Tsang style ziggurat with a precomputed 129-edge (128-layer) table. A single URNG draw supplies the uniform, the layer index (low 7 bits) and the sign (bit 7). Most samples are accepted with one multiply and compare, marked __builtin_expect-likely. Only rare wedge rejections call exp(), and only the base layer falls back to a log-based tail sampler (both noinline).
when_to_use: Hot loops that draw many N(mu, sigma) doubles or floats from a 64-bit engine (mt19937_64 or a fast 64-bit PRNG) and are bound by std::normal_distribution's cost
Projects that want a tiny, dependency-free, Boost-licensed header and an API identical to std::normal_distribution
Monte Carlo, Brownian or Langevin dynamics, and noise injection, where sample-for-sample reproducibility against libstdc++ is not required
when_not_to_use: When you need published, verified speedups: the repo has a benchmark program (benchmark/bench_normal_distribution.cc) but no results anywhere

With 32-bit engines (std::mt19937): it then draws only 31 bits, and the uniform's low bits are the same bits that pick the layer and sign, so samples have coarse resolution and correlation between layer and value
When you need other distributions (exponential, gamma); only the normal is provided
When you need sequences identical to std::normal_distribution, for example regression tests seeded against libstdc++ output
When you need long-term maintenance: last commit 2018, 14 commits, 4 stars, CI on the defunct travis-ci.org

integration.thread_safety: Not documented; the distribution object is stateless apart from its parameters (reset() is a no-op), so sharing it is safe as long as each thread uses its own URNG

gotchas: Bit budget comes from log2(URNG::max()-URNG::min()), so a 64-bit engine yields 63 bits and std::mt19937 yields 31; with doubles from a 32-bit engine, canonicalize uses all 31 bits, including the 8 bits that also choose the layer and sign
The benchmark Makefile builds with -funsafe-math-optimizations -mtune=native -O2, so any number you measure with it is not under default flags
The license is stated in the header and README badge; the README's LICENSE.txt link returns 404, so keep the header notice when vendoring
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Randompack when you want a single header that keeps your existing std URNG and std::normal_distribution call sites; Randompack is a larger library with its own engines but has published measurements. Randen, Romu, SIMDxorshift and Squares are uniform bit generators, not normal samplers, so they pair with this rather than compete with it.
verified_claims_summary: No measurement is published. The repo includes a benchmark that times 10 million draws (ns/gen) of std::normal_distribution against the ziggurat for mt19937_64, mt19937 and JSF64 with double and float, built with C++11 -O2 -mtune=native -funsafe-math-optimizations, but it records no results, compiler or hardware.
status_note: Abandoned since November 2018, but a single Boost-licensed header with no dependencies, so it is easy to vendor and audit; treat the speedup as unverified.
